In the “enigmas of visual equations” of Barja’s commentary-constructions, the author highlights the condensation of meanings whose tool is humour. trecho.2: Joseph, religious animal: Challenged to propose his version of the contemporary gaze around Joseph Beuys, Barja proposed another box/animal, or a zoomorphized tabernacle (perhaps radicalizing the metaphorization of the term that names this small portable altar, giving it the sense of the body as a protective place of the soul). Its interior is a gilded basin displaced from its original function of a shaving instrument, receptacle of sheep’s fat. Exposed to light, it presents the variations of state of organic matter (between solid and liquid, depending on the heat and the incidence of light). mognus dei pega manet pega monet DA
trecho.3: cover herself to be Lygia Clark? ...A poetic proposal that accounts for the unexpectedness of the fact (which is real). Another tombstone, perhaps. A FIKE that unthreads the threads of the proposal of modernity taken to the extreme (its end). The yellow, blue and red ribbons, a fitting homage to the one who challenged these extremes and eliminated the frontiers between art and the (other) things of the world (with their many other threads unthreaded in various works). What to leave to the world, Mondrian? Yellow, blue and red ribbons that appear recurrently as a metaphor for a thought about (of) painting, as in De Onde Vem a Escuridão or in “Pega Manet” [4]. In the first work, they are links between the parts that do not necessarily converse among themselves, they are the (impossible) support of the concrete swing/bar NEO and they are the water of the fountain that comes out of the mouth of the Baroque lion on the black screen from which the head projects itself... Or a possible path between the inscription in expressive excess and the illusion of the economy of the minimum, pure colour and orthogonal form (a path travelled by the same strips of the work for Lygia).
